bib.title: Drag Your GAN: Interactive Point-based Manipulation on the Generative Image Manifold
bib.venue: SIGGRAPH '23 Conference Proceedings, August 6-10, 2023, Los Angeles, CA, USA

read.skipped: References skimmed only. Figures (images) not viewable in text; captions read.

question: Can a user drag arbitrary handle points on a GAN-generated image to precise target points, flexibly and across object categories, without extra networks or annotated training data?
hypothesis: The feature space of a GAN generator is discriminative enough to support both motion supervision and precise point tracking by simple feature matching.
contributions: Feature-based motion supervision (shifted feature patch loss) that optimizes the StyleGAN latent code so handle points move toward targets
A point tracking approach using nearest-neighbour search in the generator feature space, with no additional network such as RAFT or PIPs
An interactive GUI and demonstrations on diverse categories and on real images via GAN inversion

method.summary: DragGAN edits an image from a pretrained StyleGAN2 by repeating two steps: one Adam step on the W+ latent code (first 6 layers only) with an L1 shifted-patch loss on the feature map after the 6th block, then handle-point re-localisation by nearest-neighbour search of the original handle feature in the new feature map. The loop runs until handles are within d pixels of targets, with an optional mask keeping unmasked regions fixed. Nothing is trained; a latent code is optimised per edit.
method.task: Interactive point-based image manipulation on the GAN image manifold; point tracking on GAN-generated frames

eval.protocol: Face landmark: two random FFHQ images, move first image landmarks to second's, averaged over 1000 tests. Paired reconstruction follows Endo 2022: w1 sampled, perturbed to w2, optical flow between I1 and I2, 32 flow pixels as user input, 1000 samples. No significance test or variance reported.

limits: Editing quality is affected by the diversity of training data: poses outside the training distribution create artifacts (Fig. 14a, StyleGAN-human where most arms and legs are downward).
Handle points in texture-less regions sometimes drift more in tracking; authors suggest texture-rich handle points.
Limited to images generated by (or inverted into) a pretrained StyleGAN2; real-image editing depends on GAN inversion (PTI).
Out-of-distribution manipulation may be unwanted; latent regularisation is suggested but not studied.
Misuse risk: fake pose, expression or shape of real people; authors say applications must respect personality rights and privacy regulations.
Quantitative evaluation is on face landmarks (dlib as ground truth) and a flow-based paired reconstruction; no user study, no variance or seeds, and MD unit not stated.
Slower than UserControllableLT (2.0 s vs 0.03 s).
Future work: extend to 3D generative models.

code.snippet: L = sum_{i=0}^{n} sum_{q_i in Omega_1(p_i, r_1)} ||F(q_i) - F(q_i + d_i)||_1 + lambda ||(F - F_0) * (1 - M)||_1, d_i = (t_i - p_i)/||t_i - p_i||_2 (gradient not back-propagated through F(q_i))
p_i := argmin_{q_i in Omega_2(p_i, r_2)} ||F'(q_i) - f_i||_1, f_i = F_0(p_i)
